heading: Are sparse autoencoder features complete, stable, canonical units of the model's representation?
definition: SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of the model's representation.
summary: This is contested: toy settings where the dictionary's width and sparsity match the true features, and frequent, simple features in small models, often give stable, recoverable features, but many studies find features that split or absorb each other as dictionary size changes, shift across seeds and training data, and miss information the model uses. Evidence at 10–100B parameters is thin and does not test seed stability or canonicality (whether there is one unique set of feature units).

suggested_status.by_scale: C in toy, <1B and 1-10B settings; ? at 10-100B, where the checked verdicts with 10-100B-specific rows are limits_scope (with one multiple-choice supports result), the one challenges verdict whose condition includes a 27B model (arXiv:2608.11197) gives no 27B-specific value, and seed stability and canonicality are untested (counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size 10-100B 3, built before the checks); ? above 100B, absent from counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size.
suggested_status.reason: The full V5 claim is contested. Under general sparsity, the theoretical SAE optimum can shrink or zero known features; exact recovery requires extreme-sparsity and interference assumptions (arXiv:2506.15963#th-general, #example-vanish, #th-extreme). GPT-2 Small larger-dictionary directions decompose into multiple meta-latents, and adding novel directions improves smaller-dictionary reconstruction, despite strong fixed-width seed agreement (arXiv:2502.04878#r3, #r4, #r5, #r8). Gemma-2-2B first-letter latents miss positives whose causal information is carried elsewhere (arXiv:2409.14507#R9, #R10, #R11). These are specific counterexamples to completeness or canonical individual units. At 10-100B, the checked verdicts with size-specific rows are limits_scope or supports, not challenges. A single Llama-3.3-70B reconstruction reduces numerical and general-knowledge correctness (limits_scope, partial preservation) while preserving multiple-choice correctness (supports) (arXiv:2505.12421#r2, #r18, #r10). Gemma-3-27B content features miss Serbian more often in Cyrillic than in its Latin transliteration, with a Cyrillic-to-Latin miss-rate ratio of 1.35 at layer 53 (arXiv:2606.00356#r12; limits_scope). Crosscoder reconstructions explain a fraction 0.74 of activation variance in Qwen3-30B-A3B and 0.65 in Mixtral-8x7B (arXiv:2610.22127#r14, #r15; limits_scope). The untested-parts lines of these three studies leave seed stability and canonicality untested. arXiv:2608.11197's challenges verdict (adjective refinement removes 20–60% of base-noun latents) names Gemma 3 270M–27B in its condition, but its rows are Gemma 3 270M (arXiv:2608.11197#r9) and cross-model qualitative summaries over all investigated models (#r12, #r13), with no 27B-specific value. arXiv:2610.30474's challenges rows give no 10-100B value: arXiv:2610.30474#r11 and #r12 pool 600+ evaluated SAEs without stated model sizes, and #r13 and #r14 are one Pythia-160m SAE pair; its 14B and 32B Qwen3 results are Q1-deficit (monosemanticity) shares, given only in a not-in-rows line and tied to a limits_scope verdict, not to the redundancy challenge. Coverage is recorded in counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size and versions.V5.main_rows_by_operation; verdict categories in versions.V5.verdicts do not establish matched failed replications. counts.json was built before the checks.
suggested_status.open_questions: Independent tests jointly establishing ground-truth recovery, functional equivalence across SAE seeds, and identity across widths and extraction procedures would support a narrower reproducible claim. At 10-100B, a seed-stability or cross-width comparison on a 10-100B model would set a level there; a 27B-specific value for arXiv:2608.11197's adjective-refinement result, or per-size redundancy (duplicate-support) values for arXiv:2610.30474's 14B and 32B Qwen3 SAEs, could also bear on whether 10-100B is C. Above 100B, documented V5 tests are needed.

sources.headline: Same-size GPT-2 SAEs trained with different seeds shared 94% of latents.
GPT-2 small SAE reconstructions behaved almost like real activations under perturbation.
In the PLUTO pathology model, hand-picked cell-type features matched closely across SAEs trained on different data.
Llama Scope TopK and vanilla SAE decoders were far more similar than random SAEs.
Two-seed TinyStories SAEs shared feature subspaces far above a random baseline.
Simple single-token features matched nearly perfectly between Pythia and Mamba SAEs.

Toy SAEs at the true sparsity (L0, active latents per input) exactly recovered the ground-truth features.

A TopK SAE with true dictionary size and sparsity (L0) recovered 99.9% of synthetic ground-truth features.
An SAE on layer 33 of the protein model ESM-3 explained 96% of activation variance.
The authors state, qualitatively only, that learned features are largely universal across different small models.
Most small-dictionary features reappeared almost unchanged in larger dictionaries.
Replacing attention outputs in early-middle layers with SAE reconstructions kept IOI performance (logit difference) near baseline.
Most SAE latents fired independently, more so in wider GPT2-Small and Gemma SAEs.
Toy SAEs recovered true features one-to-one with independent features or tied weights.

A toy SAE with correctly matched sparsity (L0) perfectly recovered all 20 true features.
A BatchTopK SAE at the true sparsity (L0) exactly matched toy ground-truth features.
Probes on SAE reconstructions lost almost nothing in distribution versus the residual stream.
SAE features matched across seeds in a toy model and Pythia-70m, up to rotation.

Qwen2.5 base-model SAEs transferred to chat models with minimal reconstruction loss.

A proposed multistep-encoder SAE (iSAE-ME) was nearly perfectly stable across runs on synthetic data.

Simple amino-acid features in the protein-structure model Boltz-1 reproduced across SAE seeds.
A pretrained layer-6 SAE's reconstructions showed essentially no norm shrinkage, but swapping them in raised perplexity.
Tied-weight L1 dictionaries raised layer-2 perplexity from 25 to 40.
Absorption (specific latents taking over general features) rose with sparsity and width in Gemma Scope SAEs.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: An exhaustive ground-truth inventory of a naturalistic LLM's representational variables, jointly establishing completeness, reproducibility and unique canonical identity across extraction choices.
untested.basis: The untested-parts lines of these studies distinguish consistency, stitching, conditional planted-feature recovery and human concept-list coverage from recovery of the model's actual inventory. Relevant examples are arXiv:2610.23801#r13, arXiv:2502.04878#r4, arXiv:2506.14002#R1 and arXiv:2512.10805#r1. counts: versions.V5.main_rows_by_operation records operation coverage, without establishing this joint ground-truth test.

untested.what: Dictionary-wide causal or functional equivalence of features matched across independent SAE seeds on a fixed naturalistic LLM.
untested.basis: The untested-parts lines of 10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.99 and arXiv:2505.20254 explicitly leave functional faithfulness or equivalence untested; their natural-model comparisons measure vector agreement, including 10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.99#r14 and arXiv:2505.20254#P-pythia-topk. Cross-base-model firing comparisons and cross-method token-matched interventions elsewhere do not establish this dictionary-wide same-model seed equivalence. counts: versions.V5.coverage_by_operation records measurements and interventions without their joint matching protocol.

untested.what: Empirical completeness and seed stability of dictionaries through training explicitly identified as preference/RL or reasoning-stage training. The one explicit RL reasoning-stage comparison found, arXiv:2504.02922 Appendix I.2, tests latent attribution and method dependence, not completeness or seed stability.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V5.studies_by_stage has no preference/RL or reasoning entry. The check of arXiv:2504.02922 (arXiv v4) found an explicit RL reasoning-stage comparison that the pack's stage fields do not record, with no linked pack row: Appendix I.2 compares DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B with Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B after extended RL training. Table 1 reports 59 L1 fine-tuning-only latents, of which 58 (98.3%) are classified as false attributions by Latent Scaling; BatchTopK identifies zero fine-tuning-only latents at the stated norm threshold. This bears on dictionary interpretation and method dependence at an RL reasoning stage; empirical completeness and seed stability remain untested there. Base/chat crosscoder and transfer comparisons, including 10.18653/v1/2026.findings-eacl.96, do not isolate preference/RL or reasoning stages. arXiv:2601.05679's V5 evidence is a stylized completeness argument without linked V5 result rows; its untested-parts line excludes empirical completeness, seed stability and canonicality, and its reasoning-feature experiments do not isolate training-stage effects.

untested.what: V5 tests on models explicitly documented as larger than 100B parameters.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size has no >100B entry. The named large-model reconstruction example is Llama-3.3-70B, including arXiv:2505.12421#r2. Claude 3 Sonnet and GPT-4 parameter sizes are unstated in the relevant headers and cannot establish coverage above that threshold.

wording_issues.issue: Reconstruction, recovery of known directions and coverage of a human concept list are different endpoints. A Vanilla SAE with 20 latents trained on synthetic hierarchical data (20 ground-truth features in 20 dimensions, 40,000 steps) has FVU 0.000 while cleanly recovering only 11/20 features. CLIP concept coverage changes with the reference inventory. Sparse Transformer's layer-2 SAE incompletely recovers its known basis. These measures do not establish an exhaustive natural-model inventory.

Task-relevant preservation depends on the evaluation and intervention site. A single Llama-3.3-70B SAE splice loses numerical and general-knowledge correctness. For a Qwen3-8B code-deception probe on the Qwen-Scope layer-20 residual SAE, 26% of the raw probe margin is reconstructed and 74% remains in SAE error. Reconstruction probes lose code-role counterfactual sensitivity. In LLaVA-Next 7b, image-token substitution gives a slight VQA accuracy decrease, while all-token substitution reduces VQA to near chance with incoherent responses. Probe information and behavioral sufficiency remain distinct.

Stability needs a specified object, comparison and metric. Across five independently seeded SigLIP2 BatchTopK dictionaries of 4,096 concepts, mean pairwise stability is 0.16, which the authors call low (incomplete, not shown absent against a control); each run's top-512 energetic concepts reach 0.92. Pythia cross-model decoder agreement can coexist with incomplete firing agreement after alignment. Synthetic encoder comparisons separate dictionary agreement from code agreement. Archetypal-SAE ablations show that shared initialization can produce apparent agreement without demonstrating convergence from independent starts.

A dictionary direction, its encoder activation and its interpretation are different objects. In one Gemma 2 2B example (Gemma Scope 16K residual SAE, layer 16, k=2), alternative approximately minimal decompositions from the same dictionary receive inconsistent semantic explanations. Aligned cross-domain text-embedding directions can receive different labels. Gemma content labels do not uniformly generalize across languages and scripts. In GPT-2 small layer-8 TopK SAEs, active feature instances in the two margin bins nearest the cutoff have paraphrase flip fractions of 0.941 and 0.896: retention under meaning-preserving paraphrase is severely incomplete, though not shown absent against a baseline. Directional correspondence alone does not establish invariant semantic identity.

The recovered inventory depends on width and extraction procedure. GPT-2 larger-dictionary latents decompose into smaller components. In tokenized GPT-2 small layer-8 SAEs with a per-token lookup (expansion factor 16, 12,288 features), fewer than 5% of features activate on any single unigram, with token reconstruction moved to the lookup; this shows extraction sensitivity, not that canonical units are absent. TopK and JumpReLU dense latents can form antipodal pairs that AbsoluteTopK removes. Changing only the encoder scoring rule produces limited strict overlap between Qwen3-8B dictionaries. A recipe-independent inventory is not established by these comparisons.

Uniqueness results require their mathematical assumptions. The planted-mixture identifiability theorem identifies a minimal feature set while permitting split alternatives. Another recovery theorem requires extreme sparsity and non-positive interference, with uniqueness at matched width. A synthetic circle lacks a natural canonical direction choice. The Minkowski nonuniqueness argument is conditional on the Minkowski Representation Hypothesis. None establishes unconditional canonical units in naturalistic LLMs.

Individual latents need not be distinct atomic units. GPT-2 meta-latent edits separate attributes within a city latent. Llama3.1-8B manifold coordinates can align at group level while the partition of the manifold among SAE atoms depends on SAE architecture. In qualitative comparisons, selected robot variables are tiled by multiple SAE latents. These findings require specifying whether a candidate unit is an atom, composite, group or subspace.

Repeatability, predictive association and causal function need separate evidence. Synthetic SAEs can share clusters matching no true feature. Ordinary formal-language SAE latents can correlate strongly with explanations yet show no observed generation effect under clamping. In p-IgGen layer 3, TopK latents predictive of IGHJ4 do not give predictable gene-usage steering; this cautions against reading prediction as causal role but does not test completeness, stability or canonicality. Within the same Gemma model, token-matched features have different causal necessity across SAE families or activation functions. These results limit identifying dictionary coordinates with intrinsic computational units.

method_sensitivity.factor: Encoder, scoring rule, activation function, objective and structural prior
method_sensitivity.what: RES-JB GPT-2 layer-8 features: 76% activate on unigrams. Tokenized SAEs with a per-token lookup (GPT-2 small layer 8, expansion 16, 12,288 features): fewer than 5% activate on any single unigram. These are separate measurements; the matched comparisons report only qualitative reductions. Standard versus cosine-scored Qwen3-8B layer-18 dictionaries share only 6–17% under strict identity matching. iSAE-ME reaches synthetic code IoU 0.997, but on DINOv2 its code IoU is 0.356 versus 0.519 for TopK. In the alternative bilinear-autoencoder family, Qwen3.5 atomic priors have 53% per-latent agreement, quadratic/composite priors 16%, and cross-kind comparisons 7%. These comparisons change the extraction procedure applied to representations.

method_sensitivity.factor: Dictionary width, expansion, sparsity, penalty and training duration
method_sensitivity.what: GPT-2 width changes feature novelty and decomposition. Across four backbones, 45–55% of consistent ConSDL atoms at 4× and ℓ0 ≈ 32 have at least two consistent counterparts at 16× and ℓ0 ≈ 128 (12–37% for ReLU; consistency and counterpart thresholds ≥0.7). Width and sparsity change together in this comparison, so it does not isolate width. Molecular cross-size strict recovery is strong at selected early layers but falls at layer 0 and deeper layers. In multi-task sparse-parity networks, weak ℓ1 (0.01) produces spurious continued feature splitting and excessive ℓ1 (10) suppresses features entirely; these are effective-count proxies, not feature-identity comparisons. These measurements do not identify a width-invariant inventory.

method_sensitivity.factor: Target sparsity, training history, co-occurrence and concept geometry
method_sensitivity.what: Incorrect target L0 mixes known features; starting too low can leave incorrect features after L0 is corrected. Correlation controls the sign and amount of hedging, and hierarchical features produce hedging or absorption depending on SAE width. Synthetic recovery differs sharply between constant-probability and long-tailed activation regimes. ReLU/JumpReLU recovery depends on concept separability, and TopK reconstruction failure depends on K relative to concept dimension. These factors concern the data-generating structure as well as the SAE's active budget.

method_sensitivity.factor: Initialization, centering, weight constraints and alive-feature conditioning
method_sensitivity.what: Shared k-means initialization yields Hungarian distances 0.068 in DINOv2 and 0.112 in Pythia-160m, versus independently initialized classical-run distances 0.433 and 0.200; only batch order varies in the shared-start comparison. On Pythia-70M TopK SAEs, L2 changes strictly shared alive features from under 2% to about 35% and mean maximum cosine from ≤0.32 to about 0.7, alongside approximately 90% dead latents.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training corpus, token budget, refitting procedure and evaluation split
method_sensitivity.what: Gemma-2-2B feature correspondence changes with activation budget and matching strictness; the data-budget comparison lacks a same-budget reference-seed control. Single SAE fits reproduce 27–46% of features across half-data refits, pooled across sources, versus 99–100% for a varimax rotation baseline; the refits vary data half and initialization together. Pythia-70m seed-consensus recurrence is 0.78 (±0.00 over three seeds). GPT2-small cross-dataset matching is 6.21–29.48%, versus 54.85–83.46% across initialization seeds at fixed width. Reported protein cross-model convergence falls from 0.78 to 0.45 under a homology-aware split.

method_sensitivity.factor: Alignment, matching metric, feature selection and unit granularity
method_sensitivity.what: Pythia cross-model-seed decoder matching can be high while post-rotation firing correlations average only 0.252–0.437. SigLIP2 stability is 0.16 over the full 4096-concept dictionary versus 0.92 over the top-512 energetic concepts. Boltz-1 amino-acid subspace overlap is 0.36 under firing-correlation matching and 0.85 under decoder-cosine Hungarian matching. Llama manifold coordinates can align despite weak individual decoder alignment and architecture-dependent tiling.

method_sensitivity.factor: Prompt distribution, language, script, context length and activation boundary
method_sensitivity.what: SQUAD answerability features retain performance under small template changes but transfer near randomly to BoolQ, with poorer transfer at layer 20 than 31. Gemma content-label miss rates vary with language, script, layer and labeler. GPT-2 reconstruction degrades beyond its SAE's 128-token training context. In the GPT-2 paraphrase factorial analysis, rare-feature sensitivity falls from 0.645 at active budget k=32 to 0.497 at k=128; frequency and proximity to the selection boundary also matter.

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation task, layer, stream and substituted token positions
method_sensitivity.what: Llama-3.3-70B reconstruction preserves multiple-choice performance but reduces numerical and general-knowledge correctness. LlaVA image-token substitution causes only a slight VQA drop, while all-token substitution yields near-chance performance and incoherent responses. GPT-2 IOI attention-output substitutions preserve logit difference at layers 1–6 but degrade it at layers 0, 7 and 8. VLA verdict evidence contrasts preserved π0.5 closed-loop behavior with OpenVLA failure despite high explained variance.

method_sensitivity.factor: Original versus reconstructed activation space, error handling and response span
method_sensitivity.what: For Qwen3-8B's code-deception probe, ablating the top-50 sparse-mask features flips reconstruction-space predictions 32.7% but raw-activation predictions 2.1%. ViT positional-feature ablations leave substantial exact-position information when SAE error is retained; RoPE naver ViT-B reconstruction alone raises SSDC by up to 0.214. In Gemma-2 2B SVA-RC, restoration outcomes depend on mean versus zero ablation, layer window and restored features: restoring up to 25 layer-18 features after mean-ablating last-token residual errors through layer 23 (layers 24–25 excluded) raises faithfulness from 0.13 to 0.6. Gemma 2 2B base/chat all-latent crosscoder replacement reduces KL divergence by 59% over full responses and 78% over response tokens 2–10, for both L1 and BatchTopK crosscoders.

method_sensitivity.factor: Reference concepts, readout, SAE seed and representational depth
method_sensitivity.what: Vision coverage changes with the reference concept list. In the FlatASCEND clinical transformer on INSPECT, matching across 3 SAE seeds at cosine 0.7 is 42.3% at layer 0 and 24.1%, 21.0% and 19.8% at layers 3, 6 and 9. WriteSAE (Qwen3.5-0.8B L9 H4, 3 seeds) matches fewer than 1% of individual atoms at cosine >0.9, while aggregate register/bundle class counts have CV 4–12%. Concept coverage, individual identity and aggregate class counts are separate measurements.

status_amendment.public_note: The rating for models of 10 to 100 billion parameters changed from contested to undetermined: after checking, results at that size show only partial shortfalls, one study that reports a clear failure pools a 27-billion-parameter model with smaller ones without giving a separate value for it, and none tests whether features stay the same across training runs or are canonical. The overall rating stays contested, based on results in toy and smaller models.
status_amendment.level_changed_because: The overall level is unchanged (C). Its toy, <1B and 1-10B basis (arXiv:2506.15963, arXiv:2502.04878, arXiv:2409.14507) keeps its checked challenges verdicts. The 10-100B level in by_scale changes from C to ?. It had rested on arXiv:2505.12421's Llama-3.3-70B reconstruction losses, which the checks relabel limits_scope (partial preservation). The Gemma-3-27B result (arXiv:2606.00356) and the Mixtral-8x7B/Qwen3-30B-A3B crosscoder result (arXiv:2610.22127) are also limits_scope. No challenges verdict has a 10-100B-specific row: arXiv:2608.11197's condition includes Gemma 3 27B, but its rows give a 270M value and cross-model summaries with no 27B value, and arXiv:2610.30474's redundancy rows are pooled across SAEs without stated sizes or come from Pythia-160m. Seed stability and canonicality are untested at that size. None of this is a failed replication.
